==Impacts on people==

=== Health impacts ===
Climate change may impact [[health in Turkey]], for example due to increased [[heatwaves]],<ref name="Website-2">{{Cite web |date=2025-11-03 |title=Türkiye to identify climate-linked diseases under health action plan - Türkiye News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiye-to-identify-climate-linked-diseases-under-health-action-plan-215299 |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref> especially elderly and chronically ill people and children.<ref>{{Citation|last1=Bayram|first1=Hasan|chapter=Global Climate Change, Desertification, and Its Consequences in Turkey and the Middle East|date=2021|title=Climate Change and Global Public Health|pages=445–458|editor-last=Pinkerton|editor-first=Kent E.|series=Respiratory Medicine|place=Cham|publisher=Springer International Publishing|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-54746-2_21|isbn=978-3-030-54746-2 |last2=Öztürk|first2=Ayşe Bilge|editor2-last=Rom|editor2-first=William N.}}</ref> [[Wildfires in Turkey]] were the worst in the history of the republic in 2021 and killed several people and injured hundreds. Droughts risk [[Mosquito-borne disease|mosquito borne diseases]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Polat |first1=Yeşim |last2=Yanikoğlu |first2=Atila |last3=Çeti̇n |first3=Hüseyin |date=2017-08-31 |title=Effects of Climate Change on Mosquito-Borne Diseases |journal=Anadolu University Journal of Science and Technology C - Life Sciences and Biotechnology |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=86–94 |doi=10.18036/aubtdc.296680 |issn=2146-0264|doi-access=free }}</ref> The [[Ministry of Health (Turkey)|Health Ministry]] will plan.<ref name="Website-2" /> 

===Economic impacts===
Although climate related economic losses are much lower than in the EU they increased over the early 2020s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-28 |title=Climate-related economic losses |url=https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/europe-environment-2025/countries/turkiye/climate-related-economic-losses |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.eea.europa.eu |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005130238/https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/europe-environment-2025/countries/turkiye/climate-related-economic-losses |archive-date=5 October 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Environment Minister Murat Kurum estimated in 2021 that losses due to disasters, such as floods,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Pandemic stresses need for green transformation: Minister |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/pandemic-stresses-need-for-green-transformation-minister-158332 |access-date=2021-04-29 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926160346/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/pandemic-stresses-need-for-green-transformation-minister-158332 |archive-date=26 September 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> caused by climate change would amount to billions of [[Turkish lira|lira]] (hundreds of millions of dollars).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bakan Kurum: İklim Değişikliğiyle Mücadele Raporu'nu Meclise sunacağız|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/ekonomi/bakan-kurum-iklim-degisikligiyle-mucadele-raporunu-meclise-sunacagiz/2148006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217125056/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/ekonomi/bakan-kurum-iklim-degisikligiyle-mucadele-raporunu-meclise-sunacagiz/2148006 |archive-date=2021-02-17 }}</ref> The [[World Bank]] has estimated the cost and benefits of stopping net carbon emissions, but has suggested government do far more detailed planning.<ref name="World Bank">{{Cite report |url=https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/handle/10986/37521 |title=Türkiye - Country Climate and Development Report |date=2022-06-13 |publisher=[[World Bank]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615154314/https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/handle/10986/37521 |archive-date=15 June 2022 |access-date=11 July 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> Companies which responded to the [[Carbon Disclosure Project]] in 2025 saw somewhat more climate opportunity than risk.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CDP Türkiye 2025 Climate and Nature Report {{!}} CORPORATE GOVERNANCE FORUM OF TÜRKİYE |url=https://cdpturkey.sabanciuniv.edu/en/content/cdp-turkiye-2025-climate-and-nature-report |access-date=2026-10-10 |website=cdpturkey.sabanciuniv.edu}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=6}}

According to the [[United Nations Development Programme]], decreasing rainfall is exacerbating the wide social and regional disparities within Turkey, and the gap between [[Southeastern Anatolia Region|south-eastern provinces]] and the rest of the country is widening.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkey {{!}} UNDP Climate Change Adaptation |url=https://www.adaptation-undp.org/explore/europe-and-central-asia/turkey |access-date=2021-03-24 |website=www.adaptation-undp.org |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415172620/https://www.adaptation-undp.org/explore/europe-and-central-asia/turkey |archive-date=15 April 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

====Agriculture====
[[File:Çıralı_Gölü_(Karapinar,_Provinz_Konya).jpg|thumb|[[Karst lake|Karst lakes]] like {{Interlanguage link|Çıralı Lake|tr|Çıralı Obruğu}} are drying due to climate change and excessive groundwater extraction<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Poyraz |first1=Murat |last2=Öztürk |first2=Muhammed Zeynel |date=2026-07-06 |title=Spatial distribution, hydrological status of Karst Lakes in Türkiye |journal=Carbonates and Evaporites |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=109 |doi=10.1007/s13146-026-01313-2 |bibcode=2026CarEv..41..109P |issn=1878-5212|doi-access=free }}</ref> ]]
[[File:Turkish_Agriculture,_Forestry_and_Fishing_Industry_.jpg|thumb|Wheat may be severely affected.<ref>{{Cite book|date=2020-01-01|chapter=Assessing climate change impacts on wheat production in Turkey and various adaptation strategies|chapter-url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780128195277000030|language=en|pages=43–54|doi=10.1016/B978-0-12-819527-7.00003-0|last1=Koç|first1=Esra|title=Climate Change and Food Security with Emphasis on Wheat|publisher=Science Direct|isbn=978-0-12-819527-7|s2cid=216269049|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816103558/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780128195277000030|archive-date=16 August 2021|access-date=16 August 2021|url-status=live }}</ref>|alt=large cylindrical bales in a field which has been cut, lit by a low golden sun]]
Unless global emissions are greatly reduced [[agriculture in Turkey]], such as [[wheat]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Reducing emissions could mitigate worst effects of climate change, study finds |url=https://airqualitynews.com/2019/03/14/reducing-emissions-could-mitigate-worst-effects-of-climate-change-study-finds/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408083349/https://airqualitynews.com/2019/03/14/reducing-emissions-could-mitigate-worst-effects-of-climate-change-study-finds/ |archive-date=8 April 2019 |access-date=8 April 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rojas|first1=Maisa|last2=Lambert|first2=Fabrice|last3=Ramirez-Villegas|first3=Julian|last4=Challinor|first4=Andrew J.|date=2019-04-02|title=Emergence of robust precipitation changes across crop production areas in the 21st century|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=116|issue=14|pages=6673–6678|doi=10.1073/pnas.1811463116|issn=0027-8424|pmc=6452695|pmid=30858318|bibcode=2019PNAS..116.6673R|doi-access=free}}</ref> is expected to be severely affected after the late 2030s, especially in areas with rain fed agriculture.<ref name="Hasan Dudu & Erol H. Çakmak (2018)" /> Arid and semi-arid areas are at risk of [[desertification]].<ref>{{Cite report|last=|first=|date=|title=Desertification and Erosion in Turkey|url=https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/CEM/Belgeler/collesme%20belgeleri%20arsiv/Sayfa02/CEMxBROSxINGxMAIL.pdf|website=|archive-date=22 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022133519/https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/CEM/Belgeler/collesme%20belgeleri%20arsiv/Sayfa02/CEMxBROSxINGxMAIL.pdf}}</ref> Water is lost through evaporation due to outdated irrigation techniques used by the [[Southeastern Anatolia Project]], increasing the risk of severe water shortage.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Will Turkey's thirst for dam building add an element of combustibility to a regional water crisis?|url=https://www.equaltimes.org/will-turkey-s-thirst-for-dam|access-date=2020-02-13|website=Equal Times|date=10 February 2020|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213183326/https://www.equaltimes.org/will-turkey-s-thirst-for-dam|archive-date=13 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Damage to agriculture<ref name="ipc2018">{{cite web |last1=Ağaçayak |first1=Tuğba |last2=Keyman |first2=E. Fuat |title=Water and Food Security in Turkey in a Changing Climate |url=http://ipc.sabanciuniv.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WaterAndFoodSecurity_PolicyBrief_web.pdf |publisher=Istanbul Policy Center, Sabancı University |access-date=16 September 2018 |archive-date=16 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916164315/http://ipc.sabanciuniv.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WaterAndFoodSecurity_PolicyBrief_web.pdf }}</ref> is predicted to greatly increase,<ref name="Hasan Dudu & Erol H. Çakmak (2018)">{{cite journal |last1=Dudu |first1=Hasan |last2=Çakmak |first2=Erol H. |title=Climate change and agriculture: an integrated approach to evaluate economy-wide effects for Turkey |journal=Climate and Development |date=2018 |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=275–288 |doi=10.1080/17565529.2017.1372259 |bibcode=2018CliDe..10..275D |doi-access=free }}</ref> for example due to "false spring" [[germination]] or [[blossom]]ing followed by a cold snap.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Climate change responsible for spring and winter within weeks |url=https://www.trtworld.com/life/climate-change-responsible-for-spring-and-winter-within-weeks-43363 |access-date=2021-04-24 |website=Climate change responsible for spring and winter within weeks |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428025042/https://www.trtworld.com/life/climate-change-responsible-for-spring-and-winter-within-weeks-43363 |archive-date=28 April 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> The increase in early blooming, which is happening due to climate change, can be a problem for crops such as fruit trees.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Climate change bares its many faces in Turkey|url=https://www.trtworld.com/life/climate-change-bares-its-many-faces-in-turkey-42852|access-date=2021-04-29|website=Climate change bares its many faces in Turkey|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215180047/https://www.trtworld.com/life/climate-change-bares-its-many-faces-in-turkey-42852|archive-date=15 December 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Turkish wine|Vineyards in Thrace]] are being affected.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gurbey|first=Alev Perihan|date=July 2020|title=Climate Change Problems in Agricultural Landscape Areas: Eastern Thrace Vineyards|journal=Journal of Environmental Protection and Ecology |volume=21 |pages=1090–1097 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342736330}}</ref> 

A significant decline in agricultural production is transmitted throughout the economy and reduces national welfare.<ref name="Hasan Dudu & Erol H. Çakmak (2018)" /> More [[Agricultural technology|agritech]] co-operation with the EU and [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]] has been suggested.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Climate Change Threatens Turkey's Role as a Food Supplier to Europe and the Middle East |url=https://www.turkeyanalyst.org/publications/turkey-analyst-articles/item/710-climate-change-threatens-turkey%E2%80%99s-role-as-a-food-supplier-to-europe-and-the-middle-east.html |access-date=2023-12-16 |website=www.turkeyanalyst.org |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240220062510/https://www.turkeyanalyst.org/publications/turkey-analyst-articles/item/710-climate-change-threatens-turkey%E2%80%99s-role-as-a-food-supplier-to-europe-and-the-middle-east.html |archive-date=20 February 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Fisheries and aquaculture====
[[File:Engraulis encrasicol, Istanbul.jpg|thumb|[[Anchovies]] may no longer grow properly in Turkish waters.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Commercial fishing of anchovy banned for 10 days|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/commercial-fishing-of-anchovy-banned-for-10-days-161483|access-date=2021-04-25|website=Hürriyet Daily News|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260610100533/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/commercial-fishing-of-anchovy-banned-for-10-days-161483|archive-date=10 June 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>|alt=small silver fish in open polystyrene boxes labelled "Karadeniz hamsi kilo 7 lira"]]
Warming seas and [[Lessepsian migration|invasive marine species, such as from the Red Sea]], have received little media coverage. [[Fishing in Turkey|Fishing]] in the [[Black Sea]] is sensitive to the impacts of climate change,<ref>{{Cite book |editor1=Barange, Manuel |editor2=Bahri, Tarûb |editor3=Beveridge, Malcolm C. M. |editor4=Cochrane, K. L. |editor5=Funge Smith, S. (Simon) |editor6=Poulain, Florence |title=Impacts of climate change on fisheries and aquaculture: synthesis of current knowledge, adaptation and mitigation options |year=2018 |location=Rome |publisher=[[Food and Agriculture Organization|Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations]] |isbn=978-92-5-130607-9 |oclc=1078885208 }}</ref> and according to the Turkish Marine Research Foundation all Turkish seas will be affected.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Climate Change and Turkish Seas |work=[[TÜDAV]]|date=22 April 2018|url=https://tudav.org/en/our-fields/climate-change/climate-change-and-turkish-seas/|access-date=2021-04-25|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229025800/https://tudav.org/en/our-fields/climate-change/climate-change-and-turkish-seas/|archive-date=29 February 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marine Aquaculture in Turkey: Advancements and Management|url=http://tudav.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Marine_Aquaculture_in_Turkey_2020_low.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201229163801/http://tudav.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Marine_Aquaculture_in_Turkey_2020_low.pdf |archive-date=2020-12-29 }}</ref> [[Lake Van]] is shrinking due to climate change.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Türkiye's largest lake 'shrinking at dangerous levels' |url=https://bianet.org/haber/turkiye-s-largest-lake-shrinking-at-dangerous-levels-270458 |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=[[Bianet]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215130110/https://bianet.org/haber/turkiye-s-largest-lake-shrinking-at-dangerous-levels-270458 |archive-date=15 December 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Tourism====
[[Tourism in Turkey]] may become too hot in the summer for some people, for example [[Antalya]] could become too hot for some visitors during some school holidays.<ref>{{Cite web|title=How hot summers and disease could impact tourism in the Mediterranean {{!}} McKinsey & Company|url=https://www.mckinsey.com/business-functions/sustainability/our-insights/sustainability-blog/hot-summers-and-disease-threaten-tourism-in-the-mediterranean|access-date=2021-02-11|website=www.mckinsey.com|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728141027/https://www.mckinsey.com/business-functions/sustainability/our-insights/sustainability-blog/hot-summers-and-disease-threaten-tourism-in-the-mediterranean|archive-date=28 July 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> Development of [[ski resort]]s in the [[Taurus Mountains|Central Taurus]] and eastern Black Sea region mountains may not be possible.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Demiroglu|first1=Osman Cenk|last2=Turp|first2=Mustafa Tufan|last3=Kurnaz|first3=Mehmet Levent|last4=Abegg|first4=Bruno|date=2020-08-26|title=The Ski Climate Index (SCI): fuzzification and a regional climate modeling application for Turkey|journal=International Journal of Biometeorology|volume=65|issue=5|pages=763–777|language=en|doi=10.1007/s00484-020-01991-0|pmid=32845376|pmc=8116266|issn=1432-1254|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Impacts on housing===
New highways and building concrete are hindering absorption of floodwater by the land.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why does Istanbul flood so easily? Experts explain |url=https://www.turkiyetoday.com/nation/why-does-istanbul-flood-so-easily-experts-explain-3230416 |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=Türkiye Today |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-16|title=New homes, highways boost flood risk on Turkey's northern coast|url=https://arab.news/w9vhy|access-date=2021-04-25|website=Arab News|language=en}}</ref> [[Urban heat islands]] are also a problem.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dihkan |first1=Mustafa |last2=Karsli |first2=Fevzi |last3=Guneroglu |first3=Nilgun |last4=Guneroglu |first4=Abdulaziz |title=Evaluation of urban heat island effect in Turkey |journal=Arabian Journal of Geosciences |date=2018 |volume=11 |issue=8 |article-number=186 |doi=10.1007/s12517-018-3533-3 |bibcode=2018ArJG...11..186D |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324700506}}</ref> Because of the increase in temperature, existing buildings will need more energy for cooling.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dino|first1=Ipek Gursel|last2=Akgul|first2=Cagla Meral|date=2019|title=Impact of climate change on the existing residential building stock in Turkey: An analysis on energy use, greenhouse gas emissions and occupant comfort|journal=Renewable Energy |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332213083|volume=141 |pages=828–846 |doi=10.1016/j.renene.2019.03.150|bibcode=2019REne..141..828D |s2cid=132673003 |hdl=11511/38528|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

== Mitigation ==
[[File:Greenhouse gas emissions in Turkey by sector.png|500x500px|right|alt=Graph showing that most emissions are from energy and heat production, and they have increased a lot since 1990 but decreased in 2019 and 2020]]

The [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC) defines ''mitigation'' (of climate change) as "a human intervention to reduce [[Greenhouse gas emissions|emissions]] or enhance the [[Carbon sink|sinks]] of [[Greenhouse gas|greenhouse gases]]".<ref name="IPCC AR6 WGI Glossary2">IPCC, 2021: [https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGI_AnnexVII.pdf Annex VII: Glossary] [Matthews, J.B.R., V. Möller, R. van Diemen, J.S. Fuglestvedt, V. Masson-Delmotte, C. Méndez, S. Semenov, A. Reisinger (eds.)]. In [https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/ Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Contribution of Working Group I to the Sixth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change] [Masson-Delmotte, V., P. Zhai, A. Pirani, S.L. Connors, C. Péan, S. Berger, N. Caud, Y. Chen, L. Goldfarb, M.I. Gomis, M. Huang, K. Leitzell, E. Lonnoy, J.B.R. Matthews, T.K. Maycock, T. Waterfield, O. Yelekçi, R. Yu, and B. Zhou (eds.)]. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, United Kingdom and New York, NY, USA, pp. 2215–2256, doi:10.1017/9781009157896.022.</ref>{{rp|2239}}According to [[Climate Action Tracker]] Turkey's GHG emissions are not in line with the Paris Agreement objective to limit temperature rise to well below 2&nbsp;°C.<ref>{{cite web |last=Timperley |first=Jocelyn |date=3 May 2018 |title=Carbon Brief Profile: Turkey |url=https://www.carbonbrief.org/carbon-brief-profile-turkey |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200413143655/https://www.carbonbrief.org/carbon-brief-profile-turkey |archive-date=13 April 2020 |website=[[Carbon Brief]]}}</ref>

A long-term climate strategy was published in 2024 but omits [[coal phase-out]].<ref name=":39" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Congratulations Türkiye: The 2053 Long-Term Climate Strategy is a Key Roadmap to Achieve the Net Zero Target! - MLGP4Climate |url=https://mlgp4climate.com/news/congratulations-turkiye-the-2053-long-term-climate-strategy-is-a-key-roadmap-to-achieve-the-net-zero-target |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=mlgp4climate.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":55" /> The [[United Nations Environment Programme]] says a faster decarbonisation is needed, and emissions per person per year should be cut by more than half to about 2–2.5&nbsp;t {{CO2}}e by 2030.<ref name="UNEP">{{Cite report |url=https://www.unep.org/emissions-gap-report-2020 |title=Emissions Gap Report 2020 |date=9 December 2020 |publisher=[[UN Environment Programme]] |isbn=978-92-807-3812-4 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209220237/https://www.unep.org/emissions-gap-report-2020 |archive-date=9 December 2020 |access-date=22 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>{{Rp|XXV}}{{Update inline|date=January 2025|reason=need to look at new emissions gap report published in feb 25}}The government intended to complete its review of long-term (2030 to 2050) policy,<ref name=":10">{{Cite tech report |url=https://www.iea.org/reports/turkey-2021 |title=Turkey 2021 – Energy Policy Review |date=March 2021 |publisher=[[International Energy Agency]]}}</ref>{{Rp|42}}{{efn|1=In 2015, Turkey submitted its [[emissions target]] to the [[United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change]] (UNFCCC), "up to 21 percent reduction in greenhouse gas (GhG) emissions from the Business as Usual level by 2030" and aiming to emit 929 Mt of {{CO2}} (before subtracting {{CO2}} absorbed by forests) in 2030.<ref>{{cite web|website=United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change|url=https://www4.unfccc.int/sites/submissions/INDC/Published%20Documents/Turkey/1/The_INDC_of_TURKEY_v.15.19.30.pdf|title=Republic of Turkey Intended Nationally Determined Contribution|ref={{harvid|INDC|2015}}|year=2015|access-date=22 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251221173434/https://www4.unfccc.int/sites/submissions/INDC/Published%20Documents/Turkey/1/The_INDC_of_TURKEY_v.15.19.30.pdf|archive-date=21 December 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> The country will probably meet this "unambitious" [[Intended Nationally Determined Contributions]] (INDC) which it submitted to the UNFCCC.<ref name="Climate Transparency 2018">{{cite web|date=2018|title=Brown to Green: the G20 Transition to a Low-carbon Economy|url=https://www.climate-transparency.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/BROWN-TO-GREEN_2018_Turkey_FINAL.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302090520/https://www.climate-transparency.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/BROWN-TO-GREEN_2018_Turkey_FINAL.pdf|archive-date=2 March 2019|access-date=1 March 2019|publisher=Climate Transparency}}</ref>}} and publish a new National Climate Change Action Plan with sector specific targets and monitoring mechanisms by 2023,<ref name="OECD2021">{{Cite report |url=https://www.oecd-ilibrary.org/economics/oecd-economic-surveys-turkey-2021_2cd09ab1-en |title=OECD Economic Surveys: Turkey 2021 |year=2021 |publisher=[[OECD]] |issn=1999-0480}}</ref> but as of 2025 the plan ends in 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |last=iklim.gov.tr |title=Action Plans - İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı |url=https://iklim.gov.tr/en/action-plans-i-121 |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=iklim.gov.tr |language=en}}</ref> 

{{anchor|Comparison with the European Union target}}
Unless Turkey's energy policy is changed, European Union (EU) emissions per person are forecast to fall below Turkey's during the 2020s.<ref name="UNEP" />{{Rp|22}} Since the EU is Turkey's main trading partner, a comparison with targets in the [[European Green Deal]] is important to help Turkish businesses avoid future EU [[carbon tariff]]s, on exports such as steel<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 October 2019 |title=EU mills push for tariffs on Turkish flats |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/1992413-eu-mills-push-for-tariffs-on-turkish-flats |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801065541/https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/1992413-eu-mills-push-for-tariffs-on-turkish-flats |archive-date=1 August 2020 |access-date=20 April 2020 |website=[[Argus Media]]}}</ref> and cement.<ref name=":18">{{Cite news |date=12 March 2021 |title=John Kerry warns EU against carbon border tax |url=https://www.ft.com/content/3d00d3c8-202d-4765-b0ae-e2b212bbca98 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321204949/https://www.ft.com/content/3d00d3c8-202d-4765-b0ae-e2b212bbca98 |archive-date=21 March 2021 |access-date=19 March 2021 |newspaper=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref> Public and private sector working groups discussed the [[European Green Deal]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Arseven |first1=E. Benan |last2=Baydar |first2=C. Hazal |date=17 August 2021 |title=Turkey Adopts Action Plan to Comply with European Green Deal |url=https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=1d5cf7b3-0fc7-40b1-9385-caddd2760443 |access-date=7 September 2021 |website=Lexology |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907103722/https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=1d5cf7b3-0fc7-40b1-9385-caddd2760443 |archive-date=7 September 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[Ministry of Trade (Turkey)|Trade Ministry]] published an action plan in response to its [[Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 July 2021 |title=Yeşil Mutabakat Eylem Planı Yayımlandı |trans-title=Green Deal Action Plan published |url=https://ticaret.gov.tr/haberler/yesil-mutabakat-eylem-plani-yayimlandi |website=[[Ministry of Trade (Turkey)]] |language=tr |access-date=22 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251012184527/https://ticaret.gov.tr/haberler/yesil-mutabakat-eylem-plani-yayimlandi |archive-date=12 October 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> A [[green taxonomy]] has been published,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Minute |first=Turkish |date=2026-09-24 |title=Turkey sets green investment standards ahead of COP31 climate summit |url=https://www.turkishminute.com/2026/09/24/turkey-sets-green-investment-standards-ahead-of-cop31-climate-summit/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Turkish Minute |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929194223/https://www.turkishminute.com/2026/09/24/turkey-sets-green-investment-standards-ahead-of-cop31-climate-summit/ |archive-date=29 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> but criticised for including fossil gas, cement and blast furnaces.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Taxonomy paradox ahead of COP31: ‘Nuclear energy and fossil gas are unacceptable’ |url=https://bianet.org/haber/green-taxonomy-paradox-ahead-of-cop31-nuclear-energy-and-fossil-gas-are-unacceptable-324254 |access-date=2026-10-10 |website=bianet.org |language=en}}</ref>[[File:Greenhouse gas emission and absorption by Turkey.svg|thumb|upright=1.4|Burning coal, petrol, diesel and natural gas is putting far more carbon dioxide into the air than [[Forests in Turkey|forests]] can take out. There is some correlation with the [[economic history of Turkey]], such as a dip during the [[2001 Turkish economic crisis|2001 economic crisis]].]]
[[File:Ghg per person Turkey.svg|thumb|alt=From 1990 the net emissions per person graph line rises in jagged parallel somewhat below gross emissions, until it dips more sharply in 2019|Greenhouse gas per person, before and after absorption by forests. The greater net dip in 2019 is because forest cover was resurveyed and found to be more than previously thought.]]

Turkey is aiming for [[Carbon neutrality|net zero carbon emissions]] by 2053.<ref name=":30" /> The [[World Bank]] has estimated the cost and benefits, but has suggested government do far more detailed planning.<ref name="World Bank"/> The long-term climate change strategy published by the [[Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change]] in 2024 does not specifically mention coal, but says that the "infrastructure of existing fossil fuel-based facilities will be reviewed".<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.8}}

Thinktank [[Istanbul Policy Center]] doubts that the target of 643 million tonnes in 2035 is compatible with the 2053 net zero target,<ref name=":30" />{{Reference page|page=23}} and several [[Non-governmental organization|NGOs]] criticised the 2035 target as being set without consultation and an increase on 2023 emissions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=ÜNLÜ |first=Didem Eryar |date=2025-09-26 |title=Türkiye'nin yeni iklim taahhüdü net sıfır hedefiyle çelişiyor |url=https://www.ekonomim.com/kose-yazisi/turkiyenin-yeni-iklim-taahhudu-net-sifir-hedefiyle-celisiyor/845323 |newspaper=Ekonomim |language=tr-TR |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251111042324/https://www.ekonomim.com/kose-yazisi/turkiyenin-yeni-iklim-taahhudu-net-sifir-hedefiyle-celisiyor/845323 |archive-date=11 November 2025 |access-date=22 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

=== Energy ===
{{see also|Energy in Turkey#Energy transition|Coal_in_Turkey#Coal_phase-out}}
Emissions could be reduced considerably by switching from coal to existing gas-fired power stations:<ref>{{cite web |title=Country Focus: Turkey: LNG Intake Rises [LNG Condensed] underdeveloped.<ref name=":26">{{cite web |author=Susi Dennison |author2=Asli Aydıntaşbaş |date=22 August 2021 |title=New energies: How the European Green Deal can save the EU's relationship with === Buildings ===
There are almost 10 million [[Turkish construction and contracting industry|buildings in Turkey]],<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.2.3}} and as they are the largest energy consumers there are substantial opportunities for energy savings in both new build and renovations.<ref name=":20">{{Cite report |url=https://www.tepav.org.tr/en/yayin/s/1539 |title=Decarbonization of Turkey's economy: [[biomass]].<ref name="Cementis2018">{{cite web |title=Abstract on the potential GHG emissions reduction in Turkey through the cement industry === Industry, agriculture and fishing ===

|archive-date=2 March 2019 |access-date=1 March 2019 |publisher=[[Mondaq]]}}</ref> began in 2024 aiming for 10% reduction by 2029 and  80% by 2045.<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.2.2.1}} === Carbon sinks ===
{{See also|Reforestation#Turkey}}
[[File:Orman.JPG|thumb|alt=conifer trees covering a mountainside|These existing trees are being added to by [[Reforestation#Turkey|reforestation]].]]
Turkey has 23&nbsp;million hectares of forest covering quarter of the country, though over 40% is [[degraded forest|degraded woodland.]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Resmi İstatistikler |trans-title=Official Statistics |url=https://www.ogm.gov.tr/tr/ormanlarimiz/resmi-istatistikler |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210314235459/https://www.ogm.gov.tr/tr/ormanlarimiz/resmi-istatistikler |archive-date=14 March 2021 |access-date=16 March 2021 |website=General Directorate of Forestry |publisher=[[:tr:Orman Genel Müdürlüğü]] |language=tr}}</ref> [[Forest in Turkey|Turkey's forests]] are its main [[carbon sink]] and offset 55 Mt of the country's emissions in 2024.<ref name="2026table" />{{Reference page|page=table 4 B11}} The government said in 2015 that by 2050 "forests are envisioned to stretch across over four-fifths of the country's territory".<ref>{{cite news |last=Ngalame |first=Elias Ntungwe |date=29 October 2015 |title=What can Africa learn from Turkey's reforestation? |url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2015/10/what-can-africa-learn-from-turkeys-reforestation/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122192832/https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2015/10/what-can-africa-learn-from-turkeys-reforestation/ |archive-date=22 January 2019 |access-date=24 February 2019 |publisher=[[World Economic Forum]]}}</ref> However warmer and drier air in the south and west may make it difficult to sustain the present forest cover.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ömer Lütfi |first=Şen |title=Province-based Forest Cover (%) |url=http://climatechangeinturkey.com/effects-of-climate-change-forests.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180517191309/http://climatechangeinturkey.com/effects-of-climate-change-forests.html |archive-date=17 May 2018 |access-date=24 February 2019 |website=Climate Change in Turkey}}</ref> Due to forest fires and reduced productivity due to climate change trees are becoming less of a sink but,<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.2.7}} despite regional variations, forests are expected to remain an overall carbon sink.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berberoglu |first1=Suha |last2=Donmez |first2=Cenk |last3=Cilek |first3=Ahmet |date=5 April 2021 |title=Modelling climate change impacts on regional net primary productivity in Turkey |journal=[[Environmental Monitoring and Assessment]] |language=en |volume=193 |issue=5 |page=242 |bibcode=2021EMnAs.193..242B |doi=10.1007/s10661-021-09031-z |issn=1573-2959 |pmid=33818693 |s2cid=233026508}}</ref> Almost all Turkey's forest land belongs to the state and cannot be privatised. Private [[afforestation]] permits have been issued however, to encourage tree planting in areas where tree density is low.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gençay |first=Gökçe |date=1 July 2020 |title=Legal framework of private afforestation: The case of Turkey |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264837719320794 |url-status=live |journal=Land Use Policy |volume=96 |bibcode=2020LUPol..9604673G |doi=10.1016/j.landusepol.2020.104673 |issn=0264-8377 |s2cid=218962170 |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417022706/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0264837719320794 |archive-date=17 April 2021 |access-date=16 March 2021 |article-number=104673}}</ref> [[Non-governmental organization|Civil society organization]]s, such as the [[Turkish Foundation for Combating Soil Erosion]] and the [[Foresters' Association of Turkey]], are also encouraging reforestation.<ref>{{cite web |title=Forester's Association of Turkey |url=https://www.ormancilardernegi.org/en/index.asp |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422120149/http://www.ormancilardernegi.org/en/index.asp |archive-date=22 April 2018 |access-date=22 March 2021 |website=[[Foresters' Association of Turkey]]}}</ref> In 2019, an annual "National Forestation Day" every 11 November was established by President Erdoğan.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Turkey plants 11 million saplings on National Forestation Day |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-plants-11-million-saplings-for-greener-future-148558 |access-date=16 May 2021 |newspaper=[[Hürriyet Daily News]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516071918/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-plants-11-million-saplings-for-greener-future-148558 |archive-date=16 May 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Junipers]] have been suggested for reforestation because of their hardiness, but are said to need help to regrow quickly.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yücedağ |first1=Cengiz |last2=Ayan |first2=Sezgin |last3=Farhat |first3=Perla |last4=Özel |first4=Halil Barış |date=2021 |title=Juniperus L. for Restoration of Degraded Forest Lands in Turkey |journal=South-East European Forestry |volume=12 |issue=1 |doi=10.15177/seefor.21-01 |doi-broken-date=17 September 2026 |doi-access=free}}</ref> But, according to [[Ege University]] associate professor Serdar Gökhan Senol, the [[Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (Turkey)|Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry]] sometimes replants when it should wait for regrowth instead.<ref>{{cite web |last=Verri |first=Selene |date=7 January 2020 |title=Wildfires in Izmir: a green plan for the city, an urban plan for the forests |url=http://www.youris.com/environment/biodiversity/wildfires-in-izmir-a-green-plan-for-the-city-an-urban-plan-for-the-forests.kl |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125081231/http://www.youris.com/environment/biodiversity/wildfires-in-izmir-a-green-plan-for-the-city-an-urban-plan-for-the-forests.kl |archive-date=25 January 2020 |access-date=21 January 2020 |website=youris.com}}</ref> In 2023 about 15 Mt was locked up in [[wood products]].{{Reference page|page=337}}{{Better source needed|reason=This from report published 2025 need to check and cite next report in April 2026|date=January 2026}} [[Wildfires in Turkey|Wildfires]] emit carbon dioxide such as 10 Mt in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-28 |title=Greenhouse gas emissions and removals in land and forests |url=https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/europe-environment-2025/countries/turkiye/lulucf-emissions |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=www.eea.europa.eu |language=en}}</ref>

[[Soil in Turkey]] contains [[soil organic carbon]], which is estimated to total 3.5&nbsp;billion tonnes at {{convert|30|cm}} soil depth, with 36&nbsp;t/ha in [[Agriculture in Turkey|agricultural]] fields.<ref name=":22">{{Cite report |url=https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/CEM/Belgeler/yay%C4%B1nlar/yay%C4%B1nlar%202018/Karbon%20Proje%2027Eyl%C3%BCl2018.pdf |title=Toprak Organik Karbonu Projesi Teknik Özet |trans-title=Sol Organic Carbon Project technical summary |last=Karagöz |year=2018 |publisher=[[Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (Turkey)|Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry]] |display-authors=et al |lang=tr}}</ref> Soil organic carbon has been mapped:<ref name="FAO">{{cite journal |last1=Sonmez |display-authors=et al |date=March 2017 |title=Turkey's National Geospatial |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011172947/http://www.fao.org/3/a-br972e.pdf |archive-date=11 October 2018 |access-date=24 February 2019}}</ref><ref name=":22" /> this is important because carbon emissions from soil are directly related to climate change, but vary according to soil interaction<ref>{{Cite report |url=http://www.toprak.org.tr/files/Proceeding-Soil-2019.pdf |editor1-last=Namlı |editor1-first=Dr. Ayten |editor2-last=Turgay |editor2-first=Prof. Dr. Oğuz Can |editor3-last=Akça |editor3-first=Muhittin Onur}}</ref>{{Rp|107}} with low levels of soil organic carbon increasing the risk of [[soil erosion]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berberoglu |first1=Suha |last2=Cilek |first2=Ahmet |last3=Kirkby |first3=Mike |last4=Irvine |first4=Brian |last5=Donmez |first5=Cenk |date=7 July 2020 |title=Spatial and temporal evaluation of soil erosion in Turkey under climate change scenarios using the Pan-European Soil Erosion Risk Assessment (PESERA) model |bibcode=2020EMnAs.192..491B |doi=10.1007/s10661-020-08429-5 |issn=1573-2959 |pmid=32638113 |s2cid=220375323}}</ref> Turkey is a major producer of [[marble]]; it has been suggested that waste from the |last3=Ali |first3=Majid |last4=Zhao |first4=Ming |last5=Iqbal |first5=Naseem |last6=Khan |first6=Rashid |title=Recycling waste-derived marble powder for CO<sub>2</sub> capture === Economics ===
{{See also|Air pollution in Turkey#Economics}}

[[File:Co2-emissions-and-gdp.png|thumb|Recent economic growth emits less carbon dioxide]]

During the late 20th and early 21st centuries, growth of the [[Economy of Turkey|Turkish economy]], and to a lesser extent population, caused increased emissions from electricity generation,<ref name="rep4">{{cite report |url=https://unfccc.int/documents/271050 |title=Turkey's fourth biennial report |date=December 2019 |work=[[Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning (Turkey)|Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning]]}}</ref>{{Rp|10,11}} industry and construction,<ref name="CAT2019">{{cite report |url=https://climateactiontracker.org/documents/672/CAT_2019-11-29_ScalingUp_TURKEY_FullReport_ENG.pdf |title=Scaling Up Climate Action series: Turkey |year=2019 |publisher=Climate Action Tracker}}</ref>{{Rp|59–62}} as described by the [[Environmental Kuznets curve|environmental Kuznets curve hypothesis]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kılavuz |first1=Emine |last2=Dogan |first2=Ibrahim |date=August 2020 |title=Economic growth, openness, industry and CO<sub>2</sub> modelling: are regulatory policies important in Turkish economies? |url=http://ikt.nny.edu.tr/files/files/haber/2019-2020/ek2020.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417023008/http://ikt.nny.edu.tr/files/files/haber/2019-2020/ek2020.pdf |archive-date=17 April 2021 |access-date=21 December 2020 |publisher=[[Nuh Naci Yazgan University]]}}</ref> And from the 1990s to the 2010s they were correlated with electricity generation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sevgül Bakaya |first1=Melahat |last2=Ağbulut |first2=Ümit |date=20 February 2021 |title=Electricity production based forecasting of greenhouse gas emissions in Turkey with deep learning, support vector machine and artificial neural network algorithms |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959652620353695 |journal=Journal of Cleaner Production |language=en |volume=285 |bibcode=2021JCPro.28525324B |doi=10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.125324 |hdl=20.500.12684/10125 |issn=0959-6526 |s2cid=229424723 |url-access=subscription |hdl-access=free |article-number=125324}}</ref> But during the 2010s [[economic growth]] and the increase in emissions decoupled somewhat.<ref name="OECD2021" />{{Rp|59}} Since the 1970s the energy intensity of economic growth has fluctuated around 1&nbsp;kWh per 2011 USD,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Energy intensity |url=https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/energy-intensity |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=Our World in Data}}</ref> whereas the carbon intensity of energy has fallen from 300g per kWh to 200g per kWh.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carbon intensity of energy production |url=https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/co2-per-unit-energy |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=Our World in Data}}</ref> Carbon Tracker says that it is possible to [[Eco-economic decoupling|decouple]] economic growth and emissions, by expanding the country's renewable-energy capacity and investing in energy efficiency with a sustainable energy policy.<ref name="CAT2019" />{{Rp|63}}

On average the consumption-based CO<sub>2</sub> emissions of one of the richest 10% of people in Turkey is more than double that of someone in the rest of the population,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Beuret |first=Nicholas |title=Emissions inequality: there is a gulf between global rich and poor |url=https://theconversation.com/emissions-inequality-there-is-a-gulf-between-global-rich-and-poor-113804 |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]] |language=en}}</ref> as richer people tend to fly more.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 September 2020 |title=Confronting carbon inequality |url=https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/confronting-carbon-inequality |access-date=17 August 2021 |website=[[Oxfam#Oxfam International|Oxfam International]] |language=en}}</ref> Turkey's high [[income inequality]] may cause higher CO<sub>2</sub> emissions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=THE NEXUS BETWEEN INCOME INEQUALITY AND CO2 EMISSIONS: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM TÜRKİYE |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/6256284}}</ref>

The long-term strategy says that public procurement will prioritize low-carbon products and services.<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.2.2.1}} Turkey has received climate finance from the [[Global Environment Facility]], the [[Clean Technology Fund]], and various bilateral funding, but is not eligible for the [[Green Climate Fund]] because of its status as a [[developed country]] under the UNFCCC.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|43}}

Worldwide, [[marginal abatement cost]] studies show that improving the energy efficiency of buildings and replacing fossil fuelled power plants with renewables are usually the most cost-effective ways of reducing carbon emissions.<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 February 2021 |title=What is the cheapest way to cut carbon? |url=https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2021/02/22/what-is-the-cheapest-way-to-cut-carbon |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321093414/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2021/02/22/what-is-the-cheapest-way-to-cut-carbon |archive-date=21 March 2021 |access-date=21 March 2021 |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> A 2020 study said that the electricity sector is key, and that low cost abatement is possible in the building sector.<ref name=":19">{{cite report |url=http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LCDTR_Marginal-Abatement-Cost-Curves.pdf |title=Technical Assistance for Developed Analytical Basis for Formulating Strategies and Actions Towards Low Carbon Development |last=Raptsun |first=Mykola |access-date=21 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920165058/http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LCDTR_Marginal-Abatement-Cost-Curves.pdf |archive-date=20 September 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> The same study said that low levels of abatement in agriculture would be cheap, but high levels very expensive.<ref name=":19" /> A 2021 study by Shura said that energy transition could increase national income by more than 1%, the largest part being wage increases due to higher skilled jobs,<ref name=":36">{{Cite web |title=Socioeconomic Impact of the Power System Transition in Turkey • SHURA Enerji Dönüşümü Merkezi |url=https://www.shura.org.tr/socioeconomic_impact_of_the_power_system_transition_in_turkey/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917182806/https://www.shura.org.tr/socioeconomic_impact_of_the_power_system_transition_in_turkey/ |archive-date=17 September 2021 |access-date=19 September 2021 |website=SHURA Enerji Dönüşümü Merkezi |language=en-US}}</ref>{{Rp|8}} such as in wind and solar power.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|58}} According to the study socioeconomic benefits, such as better health and wages, would be three times the financial cost.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|15}}

Turkey's [[social cost of carbon|carbon emissions]] are costly, even without carbon tariffs from other countries.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nuccitelli |first=Dana |date=1 October 2018 |title=New study finds incredibly high carbon pollution costs – especially for the US and India |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2018/oct/01/new-study-finds-incredibly-high-carbon-pollution-costs-especially-for-the-us-and-india |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190208114443/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2018/oct/01/new-study-finds-incredibly-high-carbon-pollution-costs-especially-for-the-us-and-india |archive-date=8 February 2019 |access-date=24 February 2019 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The short-term health [[co-benefits of climate change mitigation]] have been estimated at $800&nbsp;million for Turkey in the year 2028 alone.<ref name=":21" />{{Rp|6}} Investment in green energy is far smaller than the country's potential.<ref name=":47">{{Cite web |date=4 March 2022 |title=Turkey balks at coal phaseout amid growing energy woes - Al-Monitor: The Pulse of the Middle East |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2022/03/turkey-balks-coal-phaseout-amid-growing-energy-woes |access-date=2022-03-09 |website=www.al-monitor.com |language=en}}</ref> Academics have estimated that if Turkey and other countries invested in accordance with the [[Paris Agreement]], Turkey would break even around 2060.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wei |first1=Yi-Ming |last2=Han |first2=Rong |last3=Wang |first3=Ce |last4=Yu |first4=Biying |last5=Liang |first5=Qiao-Mei |last6=Yuan |first6=Xiao-Chen |last7=Chang |first7=Junjie |last8=Zhao |first8=Qingyu |last9=Liao |first9=Hua |last10=Tang |first10=Baojun |last11=Yan |first11=Jinyue |date=14 April 2020 |title=Self-preservation strategy for approaching global warming targets in the post-Paris Agreement era |journal=[[Nature Communications]] |volume=11 |issue=1 |page=1624 |bibcode=2020NatCo..11.1624W |doi=10.1038/s41467-020-15453-z |pmc=7156390 |pmid=32286257 |doi-access=free}}</ref>{{Rp|figure 4}} A 2023 IMF working paper says that carbon pricing can be designed to support poor people.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/WP/2023/English/wpiea2023108-print-pdf.ashx|title=Climate Mitigation Policy in Türkiye}}</ref>

==== Fossil fuel subsidies ====
According to the OECD, [[fossil fuel subsidies]] in 2019 totalled over 25&nbsp;billion lira (US${{To USD round|25|TUR|year=2019|sf=2}}&nbsp;billion),<ref>{{cite web |title=Fossil Fuel Support – TUR |url=https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |website=[[OECD]]}}</ref> nearly 1% of GDP.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|74}} Economics professor Ebru Voyvoda has criticised growth policies based on the construction and real estate sectors, and said that moving from fossil fuels to electricity is important.<ref name=":28">{{cite web |last=Voyvoda |first=Ebru |date=22 May 2021 |title=A country outside of the global climate policy: Turkey |url=http://www.observatoireturquie.fr/a-country-outside-of-the-global-climate-policy-turkey/ |access-date=28 May 2021 |website=Observatoire de la Turquie contemporaine}}</ref> According to a 2020 report by the [[International Institute for Sustainable Development]]: "Turkey also lacks transparency and continues to provide support for coal production and fossil fuel use, predominantly by foregoing tax revenue and providing [[state-owned enterprise]] investment."<ref>{{cite web |last=Geddes |first=Anna |display-authors=et al |date=9 November 2020 |title=Doubling Back and Doubling Down: G20 scorecard on fossil fuel funding |url=https://www.iisd.org/system/files/2020-11/g20-scorecard-turkey.pdf |website=[[International Institute for Sustainable Development]]}}</ref> A MWh of electricity from Turkish lignite emits over a tonne of {{CO2}}. Some electricity from these power stations is purchased by [[Electricity Generation Company (Turkey)|the state electricity company]] at a guaranteed price of US$50–55/MWh until the end of 2027,<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|176}} despite coal power subsidies being economically irrational.<ref name=":28" /> Coal miners' wages are subsidised.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|178}}

The Petroleum Market Law provides incentives for investors to explore for oil and produce it.<ref name="difiglio" />{{Rp|198}} According to the OECD, in 2019 the fuel tax exemption for [[Petroleum naphtha|naphtha]], [[petroleum coke]] and [[Bitumen|petroleum bitumen]] was a subsidy of 6.7&nbsp;billion lira (US${{To USD round|6.7|TUR|year=2019|sf=2}}&nbsp;billion), the largest of Turkey's fossil fuel subsidies that year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fossil Fuel Support – TUR |url=https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112004527/https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |archive-date=12 November 2020 |access-date=28 November 2020 |website=[[OECD]]}}</ref> Petcoke is used in cement production.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Petcoke Podcast: Turkey's cement sector in 2020 |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/blog/2020/september/14/podcast-the-petcoke-podcast-turkeys-cement-sector-in-2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201207041215/https://www.argusmedia.com/en/blog/2020/september/14/podcast-the-petcoke-podcast-turkeys-cement-sector-in-2020 |archive-date=7 December 2020 |access-date=28 November 2020 |website=[[Argus Media]]}}</ref> In other countries fossil fuel subsidies have been successfully scrapped by good communication from government, immediate cash transfers to poor people, energy price smoothing and energy transition support for households and firms.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rentschler |first1=Jun |last2=Bazilian |first2=Morgan |date=1 January 2017 |title=Policy Monitor—Principles for Designing Effective Fossil Fuel Subsidy Reforms |journal=Review of Environmental Economics and Policy |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=138–155 |doi=10.1093/reep/rew016 |issn=1750-6816 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=3 essential steps towards ending fossil fuel subsidies |url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2021/07/3-essential-steps-towards-ending-fossil-fuel-subsidies/ |access-date=19 September 2021 |website=World Economic Forum |language=en}}</ref>
