==B==
{{glossary}}
{{term|[[backcountry]]}}
{{defn|Any geographical area that is remote, isolated, undeveloped, or difficult to access, as contrasted with {{gli|frontcountry}}; sparsely populated or uninhabited {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wilderness}}. See also ''{{gli|bush}}''.}}

{{term|[[backshore]]}}
{{defn|The part of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|seashore}} lying inland from the {{gli|mean high water line}}, {{gli|landwards}} of the {{gli|foreshore}}, from which it is often delineated by a conspicuous {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|strandline}}.<ref name="Clark"/> This part of the {{gli|beach}} is only affected by waves during exceptional {{gli|high tides}} or severe storms.}}

{{term|backslope}}
{{defn|The part of the profile of a {{gli|grade|hillslope}} that forms the steepest, typically linear portion of the slope, generally located in the middle and bounded by a convex {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shoulder}} above and a concave {{gli|footslope}} below. The backslope may or may not include vertical or near-vertical {{gli|cliffs}}.<ref name="NRCS 2018"/>}}

{{term|[[backwash (physical phenomenon)|backwash]]}}
{{defn|The seaward return flow of a receding wave after it has broken on a {{gli|beach}} or other surface.<ref name="Clark"/> Contrast ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|swash}}''.}}

{{term|[[backwater (river)|backwater]]}}
{{defn|no=1|A part of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} in which there is little or no current, especially a side channel, a sluggish {{gli|meander}}, or a slowing and widening of the {{gli|main stem}} created by an obstruction to flow.}}
{{defn|no=2|A place regarded as remote, underdeveloped, or culturally backward relative to other places; a place or state of stagnation, in which little or no economic, social, or intellectual progress occurs.}}
{{defn|no=3|A secluded, peaceful place.}}

{{term|badia}}
{{defn|In the Middle East, an arid area characterized by low or irregular precipitation and little or no vegetation.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[badlands]]}}
{{defn|An area of rugged or irregular {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|topography}} resulting from extensive wind and water erosion of unconsolidated [[sedimentary rock]].<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|term=[[Bajada (geography)|bajada]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''bahada'''.}}
{{defn|A series of adjacent {{gli|alluvial fans}} coalescing in a {{gli|depression|basin}} at the foot of a {{gli|mountain range}}.}}

{{term|[[Balkanization]]}}
{{defn|The political fragmentation of a larger {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|region}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state}} into multiple smaller regions or states, often implying mutual hostility or lack of cooperation between such units, as has occurred frequently in the Balkan Peninsula of southeastern Europe.}}

{{term|[[bank (geography)|bank]]}}{{anchor|banks}}
{{defn|no=1|The land alongside a {{gli|body of water}}, particularly the sloping ground bordering and defining the {{gli|channel}} of a flowing {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|watercourse}} such as a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|An elevation in the {{gli|bed}} of a river, stream, or shallow {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}}, either fully or partially submerged, mid-channel or connected to the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shore}}, and usually made of sand, mud, gravel, or other loose sediment. See also ''{{gli|bar}}'' and ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shoal}}''.}}
{{defn|no=3|Another name for a {{gli|hill}} or hillside.}}

{{term|bankfull stage}}
{{defn|The {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream stage|stage}} during which the {{gli|channel}} of a river or stream is completely filled with water from {{gli|bank}} to bank, immediately preceding the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|overbank stage}}, when the river overflows its banks and inundates the surrounding {{gli|floodplain}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[bar (river morphology)|bar]]}}{{anchor|bars}}
{{defn|An elevated area of unconsolidated sediment such as sand or gravel which has been deposited by the flow of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} or other moving body of water. See also ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shoal}}''.}}

{{term|[[barachois]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''barasway''' or '''barrisway'''.}}
{{defn|A shallow coastal {{gli|lagoon}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|pond}}, or {{gli|estuary}} that is partially or totally separated from the ocean by a sand, gravel, or shingle {{gli|bar}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|spit}}; or the bar itself, often created at the {{gli|mouth}} of a river by the deposition of riverine sediment and {{gli|longshore drift}}. The term is primarily used in [[Atlantic Canada]].}}

{{term|[[barrage (dam)|barrage]]}}
{{defn|An {{gli|impoundment}} built for seasonal floodwater storage and/or to create a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|reservoir}} for irrigation, as opposed to a {{gli|dam}}, which instead serves the purpose of hydroelectric power generation, though the terms are sometimes used more or less interchangeably.}}

{{term|[[barrier island]]}}{{anchor|barrier islands}}
{{defn|A long, narrow {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ridge}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shoal}} lying above the {{gli|highest high water|highest high tide}} level (thereby creating an {{gli|island}}) and parallel to the mainland {{gli|coast}}, from which it is separated by a {{gli|lagoon}}.<ref name="Clark"/> Barrier islands are essentially very large sandbars deposited naturally by wave and tidal action, often in extensive chains along the coastline, or created artificially by {{gli|dredging}}. Though their size and shape change frequently, particularly during storms, they are important natural {{gli|breakwaters}}, sheltering areas of relatively calm waters where {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wetlands}} and marine life flourish. See also ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|spit}}'' and ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tied island}}''.}}
[[File:Accreting coast Image6.svg|thumb|right|400px|Diagram of various coastal landforms depicting a '''{{gli|barrier island}}''']]

{{term|[[barrier reef]]}}
{{defn|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|reef|coral reef}} lying parallel to a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shore}} and some distance from it, creating a sheltered {{gli|lagoon}} which the reef protects from the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|open ocean}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[barrier ridge]]}}
{{defn|Any steep, unnavigable {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ridge}} or {{gli|escarpment}} isolating one {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|terrain}} from another.}}

{{term|[[barrio]]}}
{{defn|In the Spanish-speaking world, a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|neighborhood}} or community within a larger urban area, generally with informal boundaries, though in some places the term may refer to a formal {{gli|administrative subdivision|subdivision}} of a {{gli|municipality}}.}}

{{term|barrow}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tumulus}}''.}}

{{term|[[barysphere]]}}
{{defn|The {{gli|Earth's core}} and {{gli|mantle}} considered together, i.e. all of the Earth's interior beneath the {{gli|lithosphere}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|base level}}
{{defn|The lowest level to which a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}} can erode its {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|streambed|bed}}. The ultimate base level of all streams is {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea level}}.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[baseline (surveying)|baseline]]}}
{{defn|An accurately measured line of known length on the Earth's surface, used as a reference line in {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|triangulation}} and other {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surveying}} operations.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[depression (geology)|basin]]}}{{anchor|basins}}
{{defn|Another name for a {{gli|depression}}, particularly one that is approximately circular, level or nearly level at the bottom, and/or surrounded on all sides by land of uniform elevation.}}

{{term|[[batholith]]}}
{{defn|A very large body of {{gli|igneous rock}}, usually [[granite]], which has been exposed by [[erosion]] of the overlying rock.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[bathymetry]]}}
{{defn|no=1|The measurement of water depth, mainly of {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|seas}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|oceans}} but sometimes of deep {{gli|lakes}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|The study and depiction of the physical features or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|terrain|relief}} of the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|seabed|floor}} of a lake or ocean. In this sense bathymetry is considered the underwater equivalent of {{gli|hypsometry}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|topography}}.}}

{{term|[[bay]]}}{{anchor|bays}}
{{defn|A {{gli|coastal}} body of water that is directly connected to but recessed from a larger body of water, such as an {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}}, {{gli|lake}}, or another bay. The land surrounding a bay usually shelters it from strong winds and waves, making bays ideal places for {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ports}} and {{gli|harbors}}.}}

{{term|[[bayou]]}}{{anchor|bayous}}
{{defn|In the southern United States, a sluggish or stagnant {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|slough}} or {{gli|backwater}}, or a {{gli|marsh|marshy}} outlet of a {{gli|lake}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[beach]]}}{{anchor|beaches}}
{{defn|A landform along the {{gli|coast|shoreline}} of an {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}}, {{gli|lake}}, or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} with a loose surface of sand, gravel, shingle, pebbles, shells, stones, or coral.}}

{{term|[[bearing (navigation)|bearing]]}}{{anchor|bearings}}
{{defn|The direction or position of an object, or the direction of an object's movement, relative to a fixed point. It is typically measured in {{gli|degrees}} and can be determined with a {{gli|compass}}. By convention, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|North Magnetic Pole|magnetic north}} is defined as having a bearing of zero degrees.}}

{{term|[[bedrock]]}}
{{defn|The solid rock in the Earth's {{gli|crust}} that underlies all soil and other loose material; the rock material that breaks down eventually to form soil.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|belt}}
{{ghat|Also '''corridor'''.}}
{{defn|A large {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|region}} or {{gli|district}} (often but not necessarily a broad, elongated area of vague or indeterminate boundaries) identified or associated with one or more particular, distinctive characteristics, e.g. of climate ([[banana belt]]), vegetation ([[Pine Belt (Mississippi)|Pine Belt]]), topography ([[Alpide belt]]), geology or mineral resources ([[Lead Belt]]), agriculture ([[Corn Belt]]), land use ({{gli|green belt}}), language or ethnicity ([[Hindi Belt]]), or social/cultural demographics ([[Bible Belt]]).<ref name="Clark"/> See also ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|regionalism}}''.}}

{{term|bench}}
{{defn|A narrow step, shelf, ledge, or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|terrace}}, typically backed by a steep slope, produced either naturally (e.g. by erosion, as with a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wave-cut platform|wave-cut bench}}) or artificially (e.g. by mining).<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[benchmark (surveying)|benchmark]]}}
{{defn|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surveying}} mark cut or embedded into a durable, fixed material, such as a rock or the wall of a building, for which the height above some designated {{gli|datum level}} has been accurately measured.}}

}}

{{term|[[wikt:berg|berg]]}}
{{defn|no=1|A {{gli|mountain}} or hill; a {{gli|cliff}} face or precipice.}}
{{defn|no=2|Another name for a {{gli|bergschrund}}, {{gli|iceberg}}, or {{gli|inselberg}}.}}

{{term|[[bergschrund]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''rimaye''' or simply '''berg''' or '''schrund'''.}}
{{defn|A {{gli|crevasse}} or series of parallel crevasses that opens in a {{gli|glacier}} when a mass of moving ice detaches and pulls away from stagnant ice or {{gli|firn}}. Bergschrunds are common in mountainous areas, often forming seasonally near the back of a {{gli|cirque}} where the ice meets a steep or rocky {{gli|headwall}}. When the rift forms directly between ice and rock, the gap is called a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|randkluft}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[berm]]}}
{{defn|no=1|A level space, shelf, or raised barrier separating two areas, often man-made and built of compacted earth. Berms often function as {{gli|dam|impoundments}}, [[fortification line]]s, or {{gli|border}} walls and other lines of demarcation.}}
{{defn|no=2|A low, impermanent, nearly horizontal or landward-sloping shelf, {{gli|bench}}, or narrow {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|terrace}} on the {{gli|backshore}} of a {{gli|beach}} and parallel to the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shore|shoreline}}, formed by waves which deposit material beyond the average {{gli|high water mark}}, e.g. during storms. Some beaches have no berms; others may have one or more.<ref name="NRCS 2018"/>}}

{{term|[[bight (geography)|bight]]}}
{{defn|A bend or curve in a coastline, river, or other geographical feature typically indicating an especially large, open {{gli|bay}} that is shallower than a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sound}}.}}

{{term|[[billabong]]}}
{{defn|In Australia, a branch of a river that is {{gli|meander cutoff|cut off}} when the main stem changes course, leaving an elongated and often ephemeral {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|waterhole}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|oxbow lake}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[biogeography]]}}
{{defn|The study of the distribution of [[biology|biological]] [[species]] and [[ecosystems]] in geographic space and through geological time.}}

{{term|biogeosphere}}
{{defn|The outer part of the {{gli|lithosphere}}, specifically the part which is also part of the {{gli|biosphere}}, from the surface of the Earth to the greatest subterranean depths at which organic life can exist.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[biodiversity|biological diversity]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''biodiversity'''.}}
{{defn|A concept recognizing the variety of life forms in an area of the Earth and the ecological interdependence of these life forms.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[biome]]}}
{{defn|A large ecosystem characterized by a distinct climate, flora, and fauna.}}

{{term|[[biosphere]]}}
{{defn|The entirety of all biological systems on Earth, integrating all living beings and [[ecosystem]]s; the realm in which biological organisms live.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[biota (ecology)|biota]]}}
{{defn|The animal and plant life of a region, considered as a total ecological entity.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[blackwater river|blackwater]]}}
{{defn|The water of a slow-moving river {{gli|channel}} flowing through a forested {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|swamp}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wetland}}, characterized by high concentrations of [[tannin]]s leached from decaying vegetation, which gives it a darkly stained color and high acidity.}}

{{term|[[blockfield]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''felsenmeer'''.}}
{{defn|A surface of broken, boulder-sized rock fragments found in {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|periglacial}} or volcanic environments,<ref name="Mayhew 2023">{{cite book |last1=Mayhew |first1=Susan |title=A Dictionary of Geography |date=2023 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |isbn=9780192896391 |edition=6th}}</ref> created ''in situ'' by processes other than {{gli|mass wasting}}, often by [[frost weathering]] in the joints of larger rocks.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[blowhole (geology)|blowhole]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''marine geyser'''.}}
{{defn|A hole or {{gli|fissure}}, especially a nearly vertical one, that is the landward opening of a {{gli|cave|sea cave}}, frequently spouting or spraying air and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|salt water|seawater}} as waves crash against the cave's seaward opening.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[blowout (geomorphology)|blowout]]}}
{{defn|A sandy {{gli|depression}} formed when [[wind]] [[wind erosion|erodes]] into patches of bare sand on otherwise vegetation-stabilized {{gli|sand dunes}} at the margins of coastal and arid ecosystems.}}

{{term|[[bluff (geography)|bluff]]}}{{anchor|bluffs}}
{{defn|A steep slope or {{gli|cliff}} marking the outer margin of a {{gli|floodplain}}, especially one formed as the river erodes the concave bend of a {{gli|meander}}. See also ''{{gli|cut bank}}''.}}

{{term|[[bocage]]}}
{{defn|A landscape of mixed woodland and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|pasture}}, with fields and winding country lanes sunken between low, narrow ridges and banks surmounted by tall, thick {{gli|hedgerows}}, especially as found in rural parts of western Europe.}}

{{term|[[body of water]]}}{{anchor|bodies of water|water body|water bodies|waterbody|waterbodies}}
{{defn|Any significant accumulation of water, either natural or artificial, on the surface of the Earth. Bodies of water may hold or contain water, as with {{gli|lakes}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|oceans}}, or they may collect and move water from one place to another, as with {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|rivers}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|streams}}, and other {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|watercourses}}.}}

{{term|[[bog]]}}{{anchor|bogs}}
{{ghat|Also '''mire''', '''quagmire''', or '''{{gli|muskeg}}'''.}}
{{defn|A type of {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wetland}} which accumulates deposits of dead plant material, especially [[moss]]es, known as [[peat]]. Bogs occur where water at the ground surface is acidic and low in dissolved nutrients. They are one of four main types of wetland, along with {{gli|fens}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|marshes}}, and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|swamps}}.}}

{{term|bootheel}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|salient}}''.}}

{{term|[[border]]}}{{anchor|borders|boundary|boundaries}}
{{defn|The geographical boundary of a political entity or legal jurisdiction, such as a {{gli|country}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state}}, or other [[subnational entity]].<ref name="OERI 1996"/>}}

{{term|bore}}
{{defn|no=1|([[tidal bore|tidal]]) A steep-fronted wave formed by the convergence of two {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tide|tidal bulges}} or by the constriction of an incoming tide as it travels up a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}}, {{gli|firth}}, or narrow {{gli|bay}}, temporarily reversing the direction of the current.<ref name="Clark"/>}}
{{defn|no=2|([[borehole|hole]]) A deep, man-made hole or shaft drilled into the ground, e.g. in mining, or for digging a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|well}} or tunnel.}}

{{term|[[bornhardt]]}}
{{defn|A bald, steep-sided, dome-shaped hill, mountain, or rock {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|outcrop|outcropping}} at least {{convert|30|m|ft}} in height and several hundred meters in width. Compare ''{{gli|inselberg}}'', ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tor}}'', and ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|nubbin}}''.}}

{{term|[[borough]]}}{{anchor|boroughs}}
{{defn|A type of {{gli|administrative division|administrative subdivision}} in certain English-speaking parts of the world. Though traditionally used to refer to a [[fortress]] or a walled {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|town}}, modern usage of the term can variably refer to any town with its own local self-government, a formal or informal subdivision of a large {{gli|metropolis}} (as in [[New York City]] and [[London]]), or an entire administrative {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|region}} (as in the U.S. state of [[Alaska]]).}}

{{term|bottomland}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|floodplain}}''.}}

{{term|boulevardization}}
{{defn|The replacement of the narrow, congested, winding streets of an older town or neighborhood with wider, more modern streets or [[boulevard]]s, often according to a carefully plotted grid layout.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[wikt:boundary|boundary]]}}{{anchor|boundaries}}
{{defn|Any line of demarcation, real or imaginary, visible or invisible, natural or artificial, with or without legal significance, which may be perceived from either or both sides of the line, indicating the place at which two or more geographical areas of distinct ownership, administration, legal jurisdiction, or any other quality meet; e.g. a {{gli|border}} separating political or {{gli|administrative divisions}}, zones of occupation, natural areas, or private and public property.<ref name="Clark"/> See also ''{{gli|frontier}}''.}}

{{term|[[bourne (stream)|bourne]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''bourn''', '''born''', '''borne''', and '''{{gli|burn}}'''.}}
{{defn|A seasonal or {{gli|intermittent stream}} flowing from a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|spring}} in an otherwise dry {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valley}}, and whose flow depends on the level of the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|water table}}; or the spring or fount itself. The term is used primarily in the {{gli|downland|chalklands}} of southern England.<ref name="Clark"/> See also ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|winterbourne}}''.}}

{{term|[[box canyon]]}}
{{defn|A short, narrow {{gli|canyon}} with steep walls on three sides, allowing entry and exit only through the {{gli|mouth}} of the canyon.}}

{{term|brake}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|canebrake}}''.}}

{{term|brash ice}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|drift ice}}''.}}

{{term|[[breadbasket]]}}
{{defn|A region of a country or other polity which supports a large proportion of the country's domestic food production (especially of wheat and other grains) due to its fertile soils, favorable climate, and/or relative accessibility to agricultural interests.}}

{{term|break}}
{{defn|no=1|Any more or less abrupt change in the profile of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|slope}} or hillside.}}
{{defn|no=2|A heavily eroded area along a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} featuring steep {{gli|banks}}, {{gli|bluffs}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ravines}}, or {{gli|canyon|gorges}}. The term is used chiefly in the plural (i.e. ''breaks'') and primarily in the United States and Canada.}}

{{term|breaker}}{{anchor|breakers}}
{{defn|no=1|Another name for a {{gli|breaking wave}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|reef}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shoal}}, {{gli|bar}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|skerry}}, or area of shallow water against which waves routinely break.}}

{{term|breaker zone}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surf zone}}''.}}

{{term|break-in-bulk point}}
{{defn|A transfer point on a transport route where the mode of transport or type of carrier changes and where large-volume shipments are reduced in size. For example, goods may be unloaded from a ship and transferred to trucks at an ocean port.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[breaking wave]]}}{{anchor|breaking waves}}
{{ghat|Also '''breaker'''.}}
{{defn|A wave of water on the surface of an {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}, {{gli|lake}}, or other {{gli|body of water}} with enough energy that, upon reaching a peak size or velocity, its crest "breaks" or overturns upon itself with a distinct forward curve, with the linear energy transforming into [[wave turbulence|turbulence]]. Waves tend to break as they enter areas of shallow water, most reliably near {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shorelines}}, where the decreasing depth of the sea floor beneath them [[wave shoaling|forces them to grow]] to a critical height at which point they overturn and the remaining forward energy is dissipated upon the {{gli|beach}} as {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|swash}}, though other forces may also cause breaking, including stormy weather and passing watercraft.}}

{{term|[[breakwater (structure)|breakwater]]}}{{anchor|breakwaters}}
{{defn|Any man-made structure built on the {{gli|coast}} of a body of water, typically the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}}, in order to reduce the intensity of wave action in an area adjacent to the shore, thereby providing safe harbourage for human activities in the inshore waters. Breakwaters may also be designed to protect the coastline from [[coastal erosion]] and {{gli|longshore drift}}.}}

{{term|[[brownfield]]}}
{{defn|Any previously developed area of land that is no longer in use, often with derelict buildings and {{gli|infrastructure}}, and in some contexts implying land that has been abandoned because of pollution or contamination.<ref name="Clark"/> Compare ''{{gli|greenfield}}''.}}

{{term|[[shrubland|brush]]}}
{{defn|Low-lying, woody, often dense vegetation or plant debris, e.g. {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|scrub}}; a thicket of small trees and shrubs, or the plant community characterized by vegetation dominated by shrubs.}}

{{term|[[built environment]]}}
{{defn|The human-made spaces that provide the setting for human activity, in which people live, work, and recreate on a day-to-day basis.}}

{{term|[[burgh]]}}
{{defn|A type of {{gli|administrative division|administrative subdivision}} in Scotland and northern England, equivalent to a {{gli|borough}}.}}

{{term|[[burn (stream)|burn]]}}
{{defn|In parts of the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand, a large {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}} or a small {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}}. See also ''{{gli|bourne}}''.}}

{{term|[[the bush|bush]]}}
{{defn|Wild, undeveloped, or uncultivated land, especially when covered by thick shrubs and vegetation; sparsely populated or uninhabited {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wilderness}}. See also ''{{gli|backcountry}}'', ''{{gli|hinterland}}'', ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|outback}}'', and ''{{gli|bushveld}}''.}}

{{term|[[bushveld]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''lowveld''', or simply '''bush''' or '''veld'''.}}
{{defn|In southern Africa, a tropical or subtropical woodland {{gli|ecoregion}} consisting largely of open {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|savanna}} with scattered trees; wild countryside as opposed to cultivated land.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[butte]]}}{{anchor|buttes}}
{{defn|An isolated {{gli|hill}} or {{gli|mountain}} with steep or precipitous sides, usually having a smaller summit area than a {{gli|mesa}}.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|bypass}}
{{defn|no=1|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|route}} which diverges around a place rather than traveling through it, especially a road or footpath built specifically for the purpose of diverting automobile or pedestrian traffic away from areas that are congested, blocked, under construction, or unsafe.<ref name="Clark"/>}}
{{defn|no=2|See ''{{gli|flood bypass}}''.}}

{{glossary end}}

==C==
{{glossary}}
{{term|[[cadastre]]}}{{anchor|cadastral}}
{{ghat|Also '''cadaster'''.}}
{{defn|A type of [[land registration|parcel-based]] land recording system containing a comprehensive record of interests in individual units of land within a {{gli|country}} or other polity, usually including a geometric description of each parcel's physical location, dimensions, and {{gli|metes and bounds|boundaries}} that is linked to legal information detailing the nature of the interests (e.g. rights, restrictions, and responsibilities), the [[land tenure|ownership]] or control of those interests, and the economic value of the land and its improvements. The cadastre is a fundamental source of data used in resolving disputes between landowners.}}

{{term|[[cairn]]}}
{{defn|A man-made stack or {{gli|mound}} of rocks, stones, or masonry, usually roughly conical or pyramidal in shape, constructed as a burial mound, to mark a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surveyed}} point, or as a {{gli|landmark}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|waypoint}} to aid {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|routefinding}} on a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|route}} that is otherwise unmarked and difficult to distinguish from the surrounding environment.<ref name="ASCE/ACSM/ASPRS"/>}}

{{term|[[calanque]]}}
{{defn|A narrow, steep-sided {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valley}} surrounding an {{gli|inlet}} formed in {{gli|karstic}} regions along the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] coast, either by {{gli|fluvial}} erosion or the collapse of the roof of a {{gli|cave}} that has been subsequently partially submerged by a rise in {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea level}}.}}

{{term|[[caldera]]}}
{{defn|A very large [[cauldron]]-shaped {{gli|depression}} of volcanic origin which forms through the subsidence and collapse of the ground surface following the evacuation of an underlying [[magma chamber]]. See also ''{{gli|volcanic crater}}''.}}
[[File:Ngorongoro topo.jpg|thumb|350px|A topographic map of [[Ngorongoro Crater]] in northern Tanzania, the world's largest inactive, intact, and unfilled volcanic '''{{gli|caldera}}''', which formed when an immense volcano erupted and collapsed on itself 2–3 million years ago. The floor of the caldera is {{convert|600|metres|feet}} below its rim and covers more than {{convert|260|km2|mi2}}.]]

{{term|[[wikt:campo|campo]]}}
{{defn|no=1|In the Spanish-speaking world, the rural countryside or the {{gli|bush}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|In Brazil, an area of level, open {{gli|grassland}} with scattered trees, comparable to a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|savanna}}.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[canal]]}}{{anchor|canals}}
{{defn|A navigable artificial water {{gli|channel}}, usually built as a conduit for human activity.}}

{{term|[[canebrake]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''canebreak'''.}}
{{defn|A dense thicket of giant [[Arundinaria|cane grasses]], often lining a {{gli|bank|riverbank}} or other body of water. The term is used primarily in the southeastern United States.}}

{{term|[[Canopy (botany)|canopy]]}}
{{defn|The canopy is the aboveground portion of a plant cropping or crop, formed by the collection of individual plant crowns.}}


{{term|[[canyon]]}}{{anchor|canyons|cañon|cañons|gorge|gorges}}
{{ghat|Also '''gorge''' or '''cañon'''.}}
{{defn|A deep cleft between {{gli|cliffs}} or {{gli|escarpments}}, or a rift between two mountain peaks, resulting from {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|weathering}} and the erosive activity of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} over long periods of geologic time.}}

{{term|[[cape (geography)|cape]]}}{{anchor|capes}}
{{defn|A large {{gli|headland}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|promontory}} extending into a body of water, usually a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}.}}

{{term|[[capillary fringe]]}}
{{defn|The soil layer lying immediately above the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|water table}}, in which water is drawn up and held within pore spaces by [[capillarity]].<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[capital city|capital]]}}{{anchor|capitals|capital city|capital cities}}
{{defn|no=1|A primary {{gli|city}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|town}} of a country, state, province, or other subnational polity, especially one that is a seat of government for the entire polity, either by law or by virtue of being the physical location of the government's offices and meeting places, or both. A capital is often but not always the largest or most economically or historically important city of its constituent.<ref name="Clark"/> A polity may have one or more capitals, or none.}}
{{defn|no=2|Any place considered to have informal primacy or importance with respect to some characteristic or association, e.g. [[Milan, Italy]] is sometimes unofficially called the "Fashion Capital of the World".}}

{{term|[[caprock]]}}
{{defn|A [[stratum]] of erosion-resistant {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sedimentary rock}} (usually [[limestone]]) found in arid areas. Caprock forms the top layer of most {{gli|mesas}} and {{gli|buttes}}.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[cardinal directions]]}}{{anchor|cardinal direction}}
{{defn|The set of four primary directions used in {{gli|cartography}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|navigation}}: [[north]] (N), [[south]] (S), [[east]] (E), and [[west]] (W). Together they form the primary divisions of the {{gli|compass rose}}. They can be further subdivided into the {{gli|intercardinal directions}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|secondary-intercardinal directions}}.}}

{{term|[[carrying capacity]]}}
{{defn|The total number of human beings that an area can support given the quality of the natural environment and the level of technology of the population.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[cartography]]}}{{anchor|cartographic|cartographer}}
{{defn|The study and practice of making {{gli|maps}} and {{gli|charts}}. A person who draws or makes maps or charts is called a ''cartographer''.<ref name="OERI 1996"/>}}

{{term|[[cartogram]]}}
{{defn|A map in which some thematic mapping variable, such as travel time, population, or [[gross national product]], is substituted for traditional measures of land area or distance such that the geometry or space of the map is distorted in order to convey and emphasize the information of the alternate variable.}}

{{term|[[cartouche (cartography)|cartouche]]}}
{{defn|A decorative panel or emblem on a {{gli|map}} or a {{gli|globe}}, enclosing the title, {{gli|legend}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|scale}}, or any other information.<ref name="ASCE/ACSM/ASPRS">{{cite book |title=Glossary of the Mapping Sciences |date=1994 |publisher=American Society of Civil Engineers, American Congress on Surveying and Mapping, and American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing |location=New York, NY |isbn=0-7844-0050-4 |url=https://openlibrary.org/works/OL19347572W/The_Glossary_of_the_Mapping_Sciences}}</ref>}}

{{term|castle koppie}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tor}}''.}}

{{term|[[cataract waterfall|cataract]]}}{{anchor|cataracts}}
{{defn|A large {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|waterfall}}, or a long series of {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|rapids}} in a river, of the type occurring in the river [[Nile]].<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|catchment}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|drainage basin}}''.}}

{{term|[[causeway]]}}{{anchor|causeways}}
{{defn|A track, road, or railway raised above a body of water or a low-lying place by virtue of being built upon a man-made [[embankment (earthworks)|embankment]], typically constructed of earth, masonry, wood, or concrete. Compare ''{{gli|bridge}}''.}}

{{term|[[cave]]}}{{anchor|caves}}
{{defn|Any naturally hollow underground space large enough for a person to enter.}}

{{term|[[cavern]]}}{{anchor|caverns}}
{{defn|A type of [[solutional cave|solutional]] {{gli|cave}} that is formed in soluble rock with the ability to grow [[speleothem]]s.}}

{{term|[[cay]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''key'''.}}
{{defn|A small, sandy, low-elevation {{gli|island}} on the surface of an otherwise submerged {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|reef|coral reef}}; a type of [[coral island]]. Compare ''{{gli|atoll}}''.}}

{{term|[[celestial pole]]}}
{{defn|Either of the two imaginary points in the sky at which an indefinitely extended projection of the Earth's axis of rotation intersects the [[celestial sphere]]. As the Earth rotates upon its axis, the north and south celestial poles remain permanently fixed in the sky (directly overhead to observers at the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|North Geographic Pole|North Pole}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|South Geographic Pole|South Pole}}, respectively), and all other points appear to rotate around them.}}

{{term|[[cenote]]}}
{{defn|A natural pit or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sinkhole}} resulting from the collapse of limestone {{gli|bedrock}} which exposes {{gli|groundwater}} underneath.}}

{{term|[[census-designated place]] (CDP)}}{{anchor|census-designated place}}
{{defn|A concentration of population identified by the [[United States Census Bureau]] for statistical purposes.}}

{{term|[[central business district]] (CBD)}}{{anchor|central business district}}
{{defn|A centrally located commercial business {{gli|district}} in an {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|urban}} area, typically containing a concentration of office and retail activities.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[centroid]]}}
{{defn|The point in a geometric figure for which the coordinates are the average values of the coordinates of all other points in the figure, i.e. the arithmetic mean position of all points in the figure; or the point with the smallest possible average distance from all other points of the figure. In geography, the {{gli|geographical center}} of a region of the Earth's surface is the centroid of the two-dimensional shape of that region, as projected radially to {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea level}} or onto a {{gli|geoid}}.<ref name="ASCE/ACSM/ASPRS"/>}}

{{term|[[chain (unit)|chain]]}}
{{defn|A unit of length equal to {{convert|66|ft|m|sigfig=5}}, used especially in public land {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surveys}} in the United States; 10 square chains is equal to {{convert|1|acre|hectare}}. Though the literal chains used to measure this distance have long been superseded, surveying tapes are often still called "chains", and measuring with a tape may be called "chaining".<ref name="Thompson 1988">{{cite book |last1=Thompson |first1=Morris M. |title=Maps for America: Cartographic products of the U.S. Geological Survey and others |date=1988 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |location=Washington, D.C. |edition=3rd |url=https://pubs.usgs.gov/unnumbered/70178836/report.pdf}}</ref>}}

{{term|[[channel (geography)|channel]]}}{{anchor|channels|strait|straits}}
{{ghat|Also '''strait'''.}}
{{defn|no=1|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|waterway}} separating two relatively close landmasses.}}
{{defn|no=2|Any narrow {{gli|body of water}} that connects two larger bodies of water.}}
{{defn|no=3|The deepest part of a shallow body of water, often used as a passageway for large ships.}}

{{term|[[chaparral]]}}
{{defn|A class of terrestrial vegetation characterized by dense, impenetrable thickets of thorny shrubs or dwarf broadleaved trees, commonly found in northern Mexico and the southwestern United States.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[chart]]}}{{anchor|charts|charting|charted}}
{{defn|A special-purpose {{gli|map}} designed for {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|navigation}}, especially [[nautical chart|nautical]] and [[aeronautical chart|aeronautical]] navigation, or to present specific data or technical information.<ref name="Thompson 1988">{{cite book |last1=Thompson |first1=Morris M. |title=Maps for America: Cartographic products of the U.S. Geological Survey and others |date=1988 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |location=Washington, D.C. |edition=3rd |url=https://pubs.usgs.gov/unnumbered/70178836/report.pdf}}</ref>}}

{{term|[[Chevron (geology)|chevron]]}}
{{defn|A triangular or V-shaped erosional microform which characteristically develops on the shallow flanks of cuestas in arid regions.<ref name="Mayhew 2023"/>}}

{{term|chimney}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|salient}}''.}}

{{term|[[chine]]}}
{{defn|A steep-sided {{gli|coastal}} {{gli|gorge}}, typically of soft eroding {{gli|cliffs}} of sandstone or clay, through which a river or stream flows to the sea. The term is used primarily in southern England.}}

{{term|[[chinook wind|chinook]]}}
{{defn|A warm, dry wind experienced along the eastern side of the [[Rocky Mountains]] in the United States and Canada. Most common in winter and spring, it can result in a rise in temperature of {{convert|20|C-change|F-change}} in a quarter of an hour.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[chorography]]}}
{{defn|The art of establishing, describing, or mapping a geographic {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|region}} or {{gli|district}}, or more broadly, the representation of space or place.}}

{{term|[[chorology]]}}
{{defn|The study of the causal relations of the phenomena present in a region; a comprehensive explanatory study of a region.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[choropleth]]}}
{{defn|A {{gli|map}} showing the distribution of a phenomenon by graded shading which indicates the density per unit area of that phenomenon; the darker the shading, the greater the density.<ref name="Mayhew">{{cite book |last1=Mayhew |first1=Susan |title=A Dictionary of Geography |date=1997 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |isbn=0-19-280034-5 |edition=2nd |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/dictionaryofgeog0000mayh }}</ref>}}

{{term|[[chott]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''shott''' and '''shatt'''.}}
{{defn|An ephemeral, often highly {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|saline lake}} that forms seasonally with fluctuations in the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|water table}}, usually in the winter, in the {{gli|desert}} basins of Northwest Africa.<ref name="Goudie">{{cite book |editor1-last=Goudie |editor1-first=Andrew |editor2-last=Atkinson |editor2-first=B. W. |editor3-last=Gregory |editor3-first=K. J. |editor4-last=Simmons |editor4-first=I. E. |editor5-last=Stoddart |editor5-first=D. R. |editor6-last=Sugden |editor6-first=David |title=The Encyclopedic Dictionary of Physical Geography |date=1994 |publisher=Basil Blackwell Ltd |location=Oxford, UK |isbn=0631186077 |ol=1419551M |edition=2nd }}</ref>}}

{{term|[[cinder cone]]}}
{{defn|A steep-sided {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|volcano}} formed by the explosive eruption of cinders that form around a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|volcanic vent|vent}}. Cinders are {{gli|lava}} fragments about {{convert|1|cm|in}} in diameter.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[circle of latitude]]}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|parallel}}''.}}

{{term|[[cirque (landform)|cirque]]}}{{anchor|cirques}}
{{ghat|Also '''corrie''' or '''cwm'''.}}
{{defn|An [[amphitheatre]]-shaped {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valley}} surrounded on three or more sides by steep, {{gli|cliff}}-like slopes and formed by glacial or fluvial erosion.}}

{{term|[[city]]}}{{anchor|cities}}
{{defn|A large human {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|settlement}}, generally with extensive systems constructed for housing, transportation, sanitation, utilities, and communication.}}

{{term|[[city center]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''city centre'''.}}
{{defn|The commercial, cultural, political, or historical focal point of a {{gli|city}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (M–Z)|urban}} area, where a significant proportion of its population, workforce, business, traffic, administration, and/or other activity is concentrated, often though not necessarily located near its geographic center. The city center may include or overlap with a {{gli|central business district}} or {{gli|downtown}} area, and the terms are commonly used interchangeably.}}

{{term|[[city-state]]}}{{anchor|city-states}}
{{defn|A sovereign {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state}} or small independent {{gli|country}} that usually consists of a single {{gli|city}} and its dependent territories.}}

{{term|clearing}}
{{defn|no=1|The practice of permanently removing vegetation, especially trees and bushes, from a {{gli|forest}} or woodland in order to use the space for another purpose, such as agriculture, civic development, or paths for roads, railways, or power lines.}}
{{defn|no=2|Another name for a {{gli|glade}}.}}

{{term|[[cliff]]}}{{anchor|cliffs}}
{{defn|Any vertical or nearly vertical rock exposure, usually formed by the processes of {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|weathering}} and {{gli|erosion}}.}}

{{term|[[cliffed coast]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''abrasion coast'''.}}
{{defn|A {{gli|coastline}} where the repeated action of ocean waves has formed steep and often precipitous {{gli|cliffs}}, as opposed to a flat or gently sloping {{gli|alluvial coast}}.}}

{{term|[[climate]]}}
{{defn|A pattern of the combination of [[precipitation]] and the [[temperature]] over time.}}

{{term|[[climax vegetation]]}}
{{defn|The vegetation that would exist in an area if growth had proceeded undisturbed for an extended period. This would be the "final" collection of plant types that presumably would remain forever, or until the stable conditions were somehow disturbed.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|clinometer}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|inclinometer}}''.}}

{{term|[[coast]]}}{{anchor|coasts|coastline}}
{{ghat|Also '''coastline''', '''seashore''', and '''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|seaboard}}'''.}}
{{defn|The area where {{gli|land}} meets a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}. Compare ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|shore}}''.}}

{{term|[[wikt:coastal|coastal]]}}
{{defn|Of, on, or pertaining to a {{gli|coast}} or coastline, i.e. a boundary or transition between {{gli|land}} and {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sea}}. Coastal areas are regions defined by interactions between terrestrial and marine processes.}}

{{term|coastal bench}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|wave-cut platform}}''.}}

{{term|[[coefficient of localization]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''index of concentration'''.}}
{{defn|A measure of the degree of {{gli|localization}} or spatial [[concentration]] of a given phenomenon, e.g. residential housing or industrial activity, within a particular space or spaces. Values for this variable, often mathematically symbolized as ''{{math|L}}'', range from 0 (where the phenomenon is evenly distributed across all spaces) and 1 (where it is densely concentrated in one space and completely absent elsewhere).<ref name="Mayhew 2023"/>}}

{{term|[[col]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''gap''' or '''notch'''.}}
{{defn|The lowest point on a {{gli|mountain}} {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ridge}} between two peaks.}}

{{term|[[colatitude]]}}
{{defn|The complementary angle of a given {{gli|latitude}}; i.e. the arithmetic difference between 90 degrees and the given latitude. For example, the colatitude of {{deg2DMS|{{decdeg|36|22|49|N}}}} is {{deg2DMS|{{decdeg|53|37|11}}}}.<ref name="Clark">{{cite book |last1=Clark |first1=Audrey N. |title=The Penguin Dictionary of Geography |date=2003 |publisher=Penguin Books |location=London, England |isbn=0140515054 |ol=3706101M |edition=3rd }}</ref>}}

{{term|[[colony]]}}{{anchor|colonies}}
{{defn|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|territory}} under the immediate complete political control of a sovereign {{gli|metropolitan state}} but otherwise distinct, often geographically, from the state's home territory. Colonies have no international representation independent of the metropolitan state and its ruling country controls its trade for its benefit. Compare ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|satellite state}}''.}}

{{term|[[colluvium]]}}
{{defn|Loose, unconsolidated sediment that has been transported and {{gli|deposited}} at the base of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|slope|hillslope}} by any of various wash or {{gli|mass wasting|mass movement}} processes, such as {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|surface runoff}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|sheet erosion}}, or {{gli|landslides}}. Typically a heterogeneous mixture of rock types and sizes ranging from silt to {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|talus}} boulders, colluvium is often derived from {{gli|eluvium}}, and differs from {{gli|alluvium}}, which is deposited primarily by {{gli|fluvial}} activity.<ref name="Goudie"/>}}

{{term|[[combe]]}}
{{ghat|Variously '''comb''', '''coomb''', '''coombe''', and '''cumb'''.}}
{{defn|A steep, narrow {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valley}} or a large hollow on the side of a {{gli|hill}} or {{gli|coastline}}, especially one enclosed on all but one side. The term is used primarily in southern England, where it often implies a dry {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ravine}} in a limestone or chalk {{gli|escarpment}}. See also ''{{gli|cwm}}''.}}

{{term|[[commonwealth]]}}
{{defn|no=1|Traditionally, a political community founded for the benefit of all or most of the members of the community, i.e. for the public welfare or the [[common good]]; or a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state}} or other polity in which the supreme power of government is vested in the people being governed; a [[republic]] or a [[democracy]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Barclay|first=James|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zo87PD4-pCUC&pg=PP242|title=Barclay's English Dictionary|date=1791|publisher=Nicholson & Company|language=en}}</ref>}}
{{defn|no=2|A free association of otherwise individual, autonomous, self-governing territories organized as a {{gli|federation}} or [[confederation]], with a jointly operated government being charged with responsibility for certain matters in the common interest, such as defense.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[compass]]}}{{anchor|compasses}}
{{defn|An instrument used for {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|navigation}} and orientation that indicates direction relative to the geographic {{gli|cardinal directions}} by measuring the orientation of the [[Earth's magnetic field]] with respect to the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|North Magnetic Pole}}. Compasses often display markings for angles or {{gli|degrees}}, which allow them to show {{gli|azimuths}} and {{gli|bearings}}, in addition to a {{gli|compass rose}}.}}

{{term|[[compass rose]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''compass star''', '''wind rose''', or '''rose of the winds'''.}}
{{defn|A figure on a {{gli|compass}}, {{gli|map}}, nautical chart, or monument used to display the orientation of the four {{gli|cardinal directions}} — North, East, South, and West — and their intermediate points.}}
[[File:Compass rose browns 00.svg|thumb|right|300px|A typical 16-point '''{{gli|compass rose}}''', showing four {{gli|cardinal directions}}, four {{gli|intercardinal directions}}, and eight {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|secondary-intercardinal directions}}]]

{{term|compass survey}}
{{defn|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|traverse}} which relies on the indications of a magnetic {{gli|compass}} for orienting the traverse as a whole or for determining the directions of individual lines.<ref name="ASCE/ACSM/ASPRS"/>}}

{{term|[[confluence]]}}{{anchor|confluent}}
{{defn|The place at which two or more {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|rivers}} or other {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|watercourses}} flow together to form one larger river or watercourse.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[coniferous]]}}
{{defn|Bearing cones; from the [[conifer]] family.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[geographic contiguity|contiguity]]}}{{anchor|contiguous}}
{{defn|The characteristic of a group of neighboring political or geographical divisions not being interrupted by politically unaffiliated land or water. Such divisions are said to be ''contiguous''.}}

{{term|[[continent]]}}{{anchor|continents}}
{{defn|One of several very large, contiguous {{gli|landmasses}} into which the Earth's land area is divided, generally by geographical or political convention rather than any strict criteria.<ref name="OERI 1996"/> Geologically, continents correspond largely to areas of [[continental crust]] on {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|plate tectonics|continental plates}}.}}

{{term|[[continental climate]]}}
{{defn|The type of climate found in the interior of the major continents in the middle or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|temperate zone|temperate}} latitudes. The climate is characterized by a great seasonal variation in temperatures, four distinct seasons, and a relatively small annual precipitation.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[continental divide]]}}
{{defn|The line of high ground that separates the different oceanic {{gli|drainage basins}} of a particular {{gli|continent}}. The river systems of a continent on opposite sides of a continental divide flow toward different oceans. See ''{{gli|drainage divide}}''.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[continental shelf]]}}
{{defn|A portion of a {{gli|continent}} that is submerged beneath an area of relatively shallow water known as a ''shelf sea''. Though continental shelves are usually treated as physiographic provinces of the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ocean}}, they are not part of the deep ocean basin proper but the flooded margins of the continent.}}

{{term|continentality}}
{{defn|The quality of being located on a {{gli|continent}}.}}

{{term|[[contour line]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''isoline''' or '''isopleth'''.}}
{{defn|A line marked on a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|topographic map}} which connects points of equal {{gli|elevation}} above or below a specified reference {{gli|geodetic datum|datum}}. Multiple contour lines, each representing a different elevation, are depicted together to show the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|topography|shape}} of the {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|terrain}} within the map area.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[contour interval]]}}
{{defn|The difference in {{gli|elevation}} between any two adjacent {{gli|contour lines}} as depicted on a particular topographic map.<ref name="Thompson 1988"/>}}

{{term|[[conurbation]]}}
{{defn|An extensive urban area formed when two or more initially separate {{gli|cities}} coalesce to form a continuous {{gli|metropolitan area}}.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[cordillera]]}}
{{defn|A long chain of {{gli|mountain ranges}} or {{gli|highlands}}, especially those formed by the same orogeny and spanning the length of a {{gli|continent}} along {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tectonic plate|tectonic}} boundaries. The term is used in particular to refer to the [[American Cordillera]], an almost continuous system of parallel ranges lining the west coasts of North, Central, and South America.}}

{{term|core area}}
{{defn|The portion of a country or territory that contains its economic, political, intellectual, and cultural focus. It is often the center of creativity and change. See also ''{{gli|hearth}}''.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[snow cornice|cornice]]}}
{{defn|An accumulation of ice and wind-blown snow overhanging the edge of a ridge or cliff face, usually on the {{gli|lee}} side of a steep mountain.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[corrasion]]}}
{{defn|The process of mechanical {{gli|erosion}} of the Earth's surface by the impact or grinding action of particles being transported across it, either by moving water, waves, glaciers, wind, or gravity.}}

{{term|corrie loch}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tarn}}''.}}

{{term|[[wikt:cosmopolitan|cosmopolitan]]}}
{{defn|Occurring worldwide; belonging to all parts of the world and free of geographical or political limitations.<ref name="Clark"/> See also ''{{gli|global}}''.}}

{{term|[[coulee]]}}
{{defn|A dry {{gli|canyon}} eroded by [[Pleistocene]] floods that cut into the lava beds of the [[Columbia Plateau]] in the western United States.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[couloir]]}}
{{defn|A narrow {{gli|gully}} with a steep gradient in a mountainous terrain, often enclosed by sheer {{gli|cliffs}} and filled with snow or ice even during the summer months.}}

{{term|[[country]]}}{{anchor|countries}}
{{defn|A {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|region}} identified as a distinct national entity in {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|political geography}}. Compare ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state}}''.}}

{{term|[[county]]}}{{anchor|counties}}
{{defn|A type of subnational division of a {{gli|country}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|state|federal state}} used for administrative or other purposes.}}

{{term|[[course (navigation)|course]]}}
{{defn|The {{gli|cardinal direction}} in which a vessel or aircraft is moving, or in which it is steered. This is not necessarily the same as the {{gli|heading}}, the direction in which the craft's bow or nose is pointed; any difference between heading and course is due to the motion of the air or water through which the vessel is moving, or other aerodynamic effects such as [[skid (aerodynamics)|skidding]] or [[slip (aerodynamics)|slipping]]. See also ''{{gli|bearing}}''.}}

{{term|[[cove]]}}
{{defn|no=1|A walled, rounded, {{gli|cirque}}-like opening at the head of a small {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valley}}.}}
{{defn|no=2|A small, narrow, sheltered {{gli|bay}}, {{gli|inlet}}, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tidal creek}}, or recess in an {{gli|estuary}}, often within a larger embayment.}}
{{defn|no=3|A small, often approximately circular, wave-cut indentation or recess in a {{gli|cliff}} on a large body of water, especially one with a relatively narrow or secluded entrance.}}
{{defn|no=4|A shallow tidal river, or the {{gli|backwater}} near the {{gli|mouth}} of a tidal river.}}

{{term|[[wikt:crater|crater]]}}{{anchor|craters}}
{{defn|Any large, roughly circular {{gli|depression}}, pit, or hole in the Earth's surface. Craters are classified into different types based on their ultimate causes; see ''{{gli|impact crater}}'', ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|volcanic crater}}'', and ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|pit crater}}''.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[Volcanic crater lake|crater lake]]}}
{{defn|A {{gli|lake}} that forms in a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|volcanic crater}} or {{gli|caldera}} (such as a {{gli|maar}}), an {{gli|impact crater}} left by a meteorite, or a crater resulting from a man-made explosion.}}

{{term|[[craton]]}}
{{defn|An old and stable region of {{gli|continent|continental}} {{gli|lithosphere}}, characterized by a thick {{gli|crust}} composed of ancient crystalline basement rock. Cratons are generally found in the interiors of {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|tectonic plates}}, having remained relatively unaffected by orogenic and tectonic activity for very long periods of time.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[wikt:creek|creek]]}}{{anchor|creeks}}
{{defn|A small, intermittent {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}} that is larger than a {{gli|brook}} but smaller than a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}}. The term is used primarily in the United States, Canada, and Australia.<ref name="NRCS 2018">{{cite book |author=National Soil Survey Center |date=2018-02-01 |chapter=Part 629 – Glossary of Landform and Geologic Terms |chapter-url=https://directives.sc.egov.usda.gov/OpenNonWebContent.aspx?content=41992.wba |title=Title 430 – National Soil Survey Handbook |location=Washington, DC |publisher=[[Natural Resources Conservation Service]] |id={{OCLC|851204093|681768549}} |access-date=2018-10-07 |archive-date=2018-10-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008022728/https://directives.sc.egov.usda.gov/OpenNonWebContent.aspx?content=41992.wba |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}

{{term|[[crevasse]]}}{{anchor|crevasses}}
{{defn|no=1|A deep crack, {{gli|fissure}}, or chasm in the ice of a {{gli|glacier}} or {{gli|ice sheet}}, or more generally in any ground surface.}}
{{defn|no=2|A break in the natural {{gli|levee}} or {{gli|bank}} of a river.<ref name="Clark"/>}}

{{term|[[wikt:crossroads|crossroads]]}}
{{defn|A place where many roads or routes of travel intersect or meet; a junction.}}

{{term|[[crust (geology)|crust]]}}{{anchor|crustal}}
{{defn|The thin shell of solid material that is the Earth's outermost layer and the outermost component of the {{gli|lithosphere}}. The Earth's crust is generally divided into two distinct types, {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|oceanic crust}} and {{gli|continental crust}}, both of which "float" on top of the {{gli|mantle}}.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[cryosphere]]}}
{{defn|The totality of water in the solid phase on the Earth's surface, including {{gli|glaciers}}; sea, lake, and river [[ice]]; [[snow]]; and [[permafrost]]. The cryosphere is sometimes considered a subset of the {{gli|hydrosphere}}.<ref name="USGS 2010"/>}}

{{term|[[cryoturbation]]}}
{{ghat|Also '''frost churning'''.}}
{{defn|The mixing of materials from various horizons of the soil down to the {{gli|bedrock}} due to freezing and thawing.}}

{{term|[[cuesta]]}}
{{defn|A long, low {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ridge}} with a steep scarp slope and a gentle {{gli|backslope}} (dip slope).}}

{{term|cultural conversion}}
{{defn|The process of cultures becoming more alike.}}

{{term|cultural diffusion}}
{{defn|The processes by which culture is spread from one region to another.}}

{{term|cultural diversion}}
{{defn|A process in which cultural groups distinguish themselves from other cultural groups.}}

{{term|[[cultural geography]]}}
{{defn|A branch of {{gli|human geography}} which studies the patterns and interactions of human {{gli|culture}} in relation to the natural environment and the human organization of space.}}

{{term|cultural landscape}}
{{defn|The physical setting created by humans that reflects the identity and culture of the area.}}

{{term|[[culture]]}}{{anchor|cultures|cultural|culturally}}
{{defn|The accumulated habits, attitudes, and beliefs of a group of people that define for them their general behavior and way of life; the total set of learned activities of a people.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|culture hearth}}
{{defn|The area from which the {{gli|culture}} of a particular group or population diffused. See also ''{{gli|hearth}}''.<ref name="IIP 2008"/>}}

{{term|[[culvert]]}}{{anchor|culverts}}
{{defn|A tunnel or conduit that channels water through or beneath an obstacle (e.g. through a man-made crossing of a {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|ravine}} that would otherwise block the natural flow of water), or any artificially buried {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|watercourse}}.}}

{{term|curvimeter}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|opisometer}}''.}}

{{term|[[beach cusp|cusp]]}}{{anchor|cusps}}
{{defn|An arc-shaped, {{gli|dune}}-like mound of sediment on a {{gli|beach}} or {{gli|foreshore}}.<ref name="Goudie"/> Cusps tend to be uniformly spaced in repeating patterns close to the shoreline, with the embayment of each arc made of fine-grained sand or gravel and the "horns" made of coarser sediment.}}

{{term|[[cut bank]]}}
{{defn|A continually {{gli|erosion|eroding}} {{gli|bank}} along a meandering {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|river}} or {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}} {{gli|channel}}, especially a bank that has been eroded into a nearly vertical {{gli|cliff}}. Cut banks generally form on the outside bend of a deep {{gli|meander}}, opposite the depositional {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|point bar}} that forms on the inside bend.}}

{{term|[[meander cutoff|cutoff]]}}{{anchor|cutoffs}}
{{defn|The new channel formed when a {{gli|meander|meandering}} {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|stream}} erodes through a narrow strip of land and thereby shortens the length of the main channel.<ref name="NRCS 2018">{{cite book |author=National Soil Survey Center |date=2018-02-01 |chapter=Part 629 – Glossary of Landform and Geologic Terms |chapter-url=https://directives.sc.egov.usda.gov/OpenNonWebContent.aspx?content=41992.wba |title=Title 430 – National Soil Survey Handbook |location=Washington, DC |publisher=[[Natural Resources Conservation Service]] |id={{OCLC|851204093|681768549}} |access-date=2018-10-07 |archive-date=2018-10-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008022728/https://directives.sc.egov.usda.gov/OpenNonWebContent.aspx?content=41992.wba |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}

{{term|[[cwm (landform)|cwm]]}}
{{defn|See ''{{gli|cirque}}''.}}

{{term|[[cyclone]]}}
{{defn|A large air mass that rotates around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure.  It can rotate clockwise or counter clockwise depending on which hemisphere it is in.}}

{{term|[[Cyclopean stairs]]}}
{{defn|A term referring to the longitudinal profile of some {{gli|glaciated}} {{gli|glossary=Glossary of geography terms (N–Z)|valleys}} which have been eroded into a series of consecutive {{gli|hanging valley|hanging valleys}} resembling stairs.}}

{{glossary end}}
